rationale: Full text: 6-month-old dog with pale, jaundiced mucosae and emaciation, Trypanosoma, Babesia and Toxocara co-infection, treated with diminazene, doxycycline and supportive drugs; did not respond and died 20 days after presentation.
Two-arm treatment comparison in dogs diagnosed with babesiosis (clinical cases), with qPCR parasitaemia before and on day 10 of treatment; meets the trial rule of thumb although signs are not listed.
Earlier note identifies it as J Parasit Dis 2016 with six smear-diagnosed dogs and descriptive clinical and laboratory findings; whether treatment and outcome are reported could not be verified.

species: B. gibsoni and other Babesia spp.

rationale: Russian/English abstract: dogs with depression, fever, icterus and haemoglobinuria treated with reduced-dose imidocarb (0.3 ml/10 kg), found usable in special cases, which implies a treatment outcome; numbers not given.
Dog with fever, anorexia, epistaxis and pale mucosae, B. canis PCR-positive with Anaplasma co-infection, treated with fluids, analgesic and oxytetracycline; collapsed within 24 h.
Twenty PCR-positive pancytopenic dogs treated with triple therapy with or without filgrastim; leukocyte rise and better survival reported in the filgrastim group.

syndromes: other: low pcv, haemoglobin, total protein
rationale: Thirty PCR-confirmed naturally infected dogs with lowered haematology randomised to imidocarb, doxycycline or both; recovery by day 21 (90%, 77%, 62.5%) and pre/post blood values reported.

rationale: Rottweiler with fever, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, raised liver enzymes, BUN and creatinine, treated with imidocarb, fluids, doxycycline and haematinic; clinical recovery within three weeks.
Aim mentions treatment of the co-infection with TVT, and anaemia and biochemical changes are reported, but the abstract gives no treatment or outcome; full text not seen.

rationale: Dog with fever, icterus, anaemia, thrombocytopenia and raised liver and renal values treated with diminazene, imidocarb and doxycycline; smear negative at one month and uneventful recovery.
Dog with weight loss, splenomegaly, non-regenerative anaemia and thrombocytopenia, B. gibsoni and T. evansi PCR-positive, responded to diminazene, quinapyramine and doxycycline.
Twelve clinically ill B. gibsoni dogs randomised to doxycycline-metronidazole plus imidocarb or diminazene; parasitaemia fell by day 15 and smears were negative on day 30.

rationale: Full text (Ukrainian): 128 dogs with acute babesiosis (fever, pale mucosae, red-brown urine) in two groups treated with diminazene (Azidin-vet) or imidocarb (Imkar-120) plus symptomatic therapy; efficacy 93.15% vs 98.2%, faster recovery and lower mortality with imidocarb.

Full text (Romanian): 10-month-old Akita with pale mucosae, low haematocrit and thrombocytopenia after low-dose imidocarb, retreated with clindamycin; qPCR load fell (Ct 29.8 to >40) and general condition was very good at reassessment.

Full text: dogs with acute babesiosis, azotaemia and raised liver enzymes given basic drug treatment with or without cryopreserved red cell transfusion; haematocrit, haemoglobin and biochemistry normalised by day 10 in the transfusion group.
ResearchGate-registered DOI with no journal; a self-deposited case report on babesiosis with acute renal failure that cannot be confirmed as peer-reviewed.
